thread:
anya: Quick sync — we have two large customer asks that impact private deploy roadmap: (1) VPC control plane with explicit egress policies and multi-region failover; (2) on‑prem packaging that supports air-gapped installs + offline package registry. Need to agree priority and minimal launch criteria for Q3 planning.
matt: Thanks. Are these from the same customer or two separate ones?
anya: Different customers. Enterprise A is pushing hard on VPC control plane and cross‑region failover. Enterprise B needs fully air‑gapped on‑prem with vendor proxies and signed packages.
sophia: Flag: control plane work overlaps with infra routing and IAM changes. Multi‑region failover implies we need control plane heartbeats + leader election logic that works over VPC peering/VPN.
raj: For on‑prem airgap, biggest technical risk is the size of model artifacts and dependency graph. We need a deterministic packaging manifest and sha256 signed bundles so offline installs can verify.
tess: Security asks: HSM/KMS integration for customer keys, audit log export format (W3C? parquet?), and a hardened offline upgrade path. Also need a clear threat model for air‑gapped mode.
anya: Proposal: split into two parallel epics but tier them. Tier 1 (Q3): VPC control plane MVP (single‑region, VPC endpoints, basic egress controls) + on‑prem packaging MVP (signed tarballs, offline registry, install docs). Tier 2 (Q4): multi‑region control plane failover, auto‑sync of manifests, more advanced attestations.
matt: Sounds reasonable. Questions: What are minimal acceptance criteria for Tier 1?
anya: Minimal acceptance for VPC MVP: customer can point at their VPC endpoints, control plane traffic restricted via SGs/NACLs, documented config for egress rules, and an SLA‑level latency target for control API (P50 < 200ms). For on‑prem MVP: deterministic package format, bundle signer, installer that can run with zero outbound access, and basic healthcheck that reports via file drop or sidecar.
sophia: Implementation note: for offline health telemetry we can use a file-based heartbeat with timestamp + signed nonce that ops can pick up. Not ideal but satisfies airgap.
raj: Packaging example snippet for manifest (draft):
```
name: redwood-package
version: 1.0.0
components:
  - runtime: 2.3.1
  - models: [rwd-7b-q4, rwd-2b-int8]
sha256: <bundle-sha256>
signature: <sig>
```
This lets us verify content offline.
tess: +1. Also add a revocation list mechanism in case a key is compromised. 
anya: Risks: resource ops for Dedicated/private teams — packaging and airgap testing adds heavy QA cycles. Need to budget a partner program lab for offline installs. Cost ask for lab + integration engineers.
matt: Do we have customers willing to sign up for early access and cover integration costs?
anya: Enterprise B indicated interest to be reference and cover part of integration, Enterprise A expects us to deliver as part of SLA negotiation. We should surface this to sales for commitment language.
sophia: Timeline estimate (rough): VPC MVP — 6 weeks (infra + docs + test harness). On‑prem MVP — 8–10 weeks (packaging pipeline, signer, installer, lab validation).
raj: Dev tasks: packaging pipeline, manifest spec, signer service, offline installer, validation harness, sample manifests.
tess: Security tasks: threat model doc, KMS integration plan, revocation flow, audit wire format.
anya: Action items: @matt own VPC control plane MVP (deliverable: config + test harness) — due 1765600000. @sophia own on‑prem packaging MVP (deliverable: signed bundles + installer image) — due 1766400000. @raj produce manifest spec + validation harness — due 1765200000. @tess produce threat model + KMS plan — due 1765200000.
matt: I can take VPC MVP. Will follow up with infra on load and latency tests.
sophia: I’ll scope packaging pipeline and propose tech choices (docker? tar+rpm?) by EOD Thu.
raj: Will draft manifest spec tonight and put it in the repo.
tess: Will start threat model and sync with security reviews next week.
deploy-bot: deploy: new thread created for epic tracking -> https://redwood.internal/boards/epic/PRIV-361
anya: OK — thanks everyone. I’ll spin up a short PRD and add the acceptance criteria above, then sync with sales for customer commitments. If anything changes ping me in this thread. :thumbsup:
